target_customer: Restaurants, cafes and food retailers (coffee shops initially)
problem: Restaurants face high labor cost and turnover (YC page cites a 130.7% turnover rate in 2020) and repetitive work.
business_model: Robotic food and beverage systems; also operates its own robotic cafe (hardware plus retail)

founders.name: Guangzhe (Jack) Cui
education: University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, engineering alumnus

founders.name: Yueming (Garrett) Yan
education: University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, engineering alumnus

technical_complexity.rationale: Combines IoT, consumer robotics, 3D printing and edge-computing order scheduling; building reliable food-handling hardware as a small team is hard.

defensibility.rationale: Hardware system and operating software take effort to replicate, but no patents or exclusive contracts found.

market_need_then: Restaurant labor cost and turnover pain per YC page; 25+ pre-orders for the system reported Nov 2021.
outcome_analysis: Yummy Future remains active years after YC S19, funded by a reported $150K YC investment and small crowdfunding rounds (about $300K by Nov 2021 and another in Dec 2025), with aggregator totals ranging from $350K to $974K. It pivoted toward running a robotic cafe and matcha concept; with no priced equity round or revenue data it has stalled at small scale rather than clearly failed.
notes: Funding totals conflict: CB Insights $350K, VCBacked $974K, Standout $3.6M, Clera $160K. $150K YC figure from a search summary of an Illinois Engineering profile. Wefunder page returned 403 and was not worked around. Founder names per UIUC; YC lists Jack Cui and Garrett Yan. Description of cafe/matcha relaunch is from a search summary and undated.
